newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro to be more dominant than mark - EU Commissioner.
newsitem.headline: Euro to be more dominant than mark - EU Commissioner.

text.p: The EU's single currency will be able to play a more prominent role than any of the national currencies, including the German mark, European Union Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann said on Wednesday.

Bangemann, one of Germany's two members of the EU executive, said the euro could over time take up some functions in world markets that are now the dollar's domain, but that the U.S. currency would remain the world's leader for the time being.
"We don't feel that the euro will or can become a second reserve currency alongside the dollar," Bangemann told a news conference.
"But we do feel it has positive effects in relation to the dollar as compared with relations between the national currencies as we now have them and the dollar," he added.
For example, goods such as the European aircraft Airbus may be priced in the euro instead of the dollar, he said.
Bangemann said the euro, due to be launched in 1999, would be a stable currency.

"I do not pretend it will be more stable than the mark but it will be a stable currency and it will be based on a much broader basis so it can function in a way which is even more prominent and stronger than any national currency, including the D-mark," he said.
"The euro is stronger than any national currency so it can (over time) take up some functions which are now lost to the dollar," Bangemann said. -- Fredrik Dahl +32 2 287 68 11
